Learning Experience Platform

One learning platform, three very different jobs to get right.

A learner clicking through a course. A test-taker racing a countdown. A marker grading dozens of submissions. All three needed to feel like one coherent product — not three tools stitched together.

RoleUX Lead, end-to-end
ScopeProfile · Assessment · Bookings
PlatformWeb
The challenge

Each of these moments already existed as its own screen, with its own logic. The job wasn't to redesign them in isolation — it was to find the patterns that could hold the whole system together.

That meant asking the same three questions of every journey: what matters most right now, what state does the user need to see at a glance, and where does control need to stay visible instead of buried in a menu.

Approach

The same process, run against three different problems.

01

User Profile

The existing profile buried what people actually came for. The fix wasn't a visual refresh — it was rebuilding the hierarchy so skills, achievements and activity surfaced first, with personalisation always in reach.

Key decision

Give every piece of information a clear place in the hierarchy, not just a home on the page — and keep personalisation controls visible in the primary view, not tucked into settings.

Before → After
Improved layout Structured hierarchy Focus & visibility Personalisation control
02

Assessment Journey

One assessment, two completely different jobs: a learner working against the clock, and a marker working through a stack of submissions. Designing them as a single system — not two unrelated flows — was the whole point.

Key decision

Mirror the status language on both sides: complete / incomplete / flagged for the person taking the test, correct / incorrect / unattempted for the person marking it. Same visual grammar, so the system stays legible no matter which side you're on.

User's view
Landing pageAll the detail needed before starting — "Start now" moves straight into the assessment.
In progressProgress & time indicator, question navigation with status, marks always visible.
Success stateConfirms a completed submission before returning to the dashboard.
Marker's view
OverviewEvery submission at a glance — click a name to open it directly.
Marking viewSubmission detail, question navigation with status, marking & feedback front and centre.
Result viewWhat the learner sees once marking is complete.
03

Bookings Journey

A smaller, more contained piece of the same system: rethinking how people book events, webinars and other offerings on the platform.

Scoped and shipped alongside the two journeys above — kept brief here since it's a smaller slice of the overall work.

Also in scope

As the only UX designer at HowNow, these three journeys were one part of the job. Everything else on the platform ran through the same process too:

  • Multi-language course upload
  • Third-party HRMS integration
  • Settings section revamp
  • Every other internal page & journey on the platform

If it touched a screen, it came through me.

What carried through

Three journeys, one set of decisions

The same three principles kept showing up, regardless of which screen or which person was on the other end.

01

Hierarchy before decoration

Both the profile and the assessment started with restructuring what mattered most — not with a visual pass.

02

One status language, two audiences

The same visual states were deliberately mirrored across the learner and marker views, so the system read as one thing.

03

Control stays visible

Personalisation in the profile, marking actions in the assessment — control lived in the primary view, never behind a menu.

Thank you

Three journeys, one underlying set of decisions — and a system that felt like one product, not three.
